chapter: Armstrong band memories, Chicago players and Baltimore
title: Zilner Randolph's impossible arrangements
summary: Z. T. Randolph wrote arrangements full of 64th notes to stump the band, such as 'Body and Soul'.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: (Inaudible) before we go any further, I want to ask you -- you were talking, I want you to tell me a little about Zilner Randolph about his arrangements, which (inaudible). You were saying he tried to -- what did you say about him?
Oh, man, he used to -- he used to get a kick out of seeing if he could stick us.

And, by that I mean, you know, he would write stuff real hard, and could he write, and, you know, like, this cat used to write like 64th notes, 32nd notes, and I never will forget. He made an arrangement on "Body and Soul" that we haven't played yet. Full of 64th notes, man, and -- but, harmonically, and everything, it was correct, because he knew what he was doing. And, he would just fall out laughing, you know.
So, I'd say, "man, why do you want to waste your time writing something like this?" You know, like -- you know, even if we played it, it don't -- it don't -- it don't make too much sense.
